subject: series
synopsis: Jeremy Whitley's charming all-ages series about a princess who decides to rescue herself from her tower rather than wait for a prince, teaming with a female dragon. A clever fairy-tale parody that prioritizes character over spectacle and makes genuinely progressive points lightly.
author: Jeremy Whitley

subject: series
synopsis: J. Michael Straczynski's Image noir about a world where super-powered Protectors have safeguarded Earth since WWII — until one is murdered. A murder mystery interrogating what decades of guaranteed safety does to human institutions.
author: J. Michael Straczynski

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Fraction and Ariel Olivetti's 2007 Punisher War Journal: Frank Castle wages war inside the Marvel Universe after Civil War, later Rick Remender.
author: Simon Spurrier

subject: series
synopsis: DC and Webtoon's vertical-scroll Red Hood: Outlaws, a digital series following Jason Todd and his crew.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's various Red Wolf series and appearances, following the Native American hero in stories that have struggled to find a consistent identity across multiple iterations since his 1972 Western Comics origins.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Boom!'s comic series based on the Cartoon Network show: park workers Mordecai and Rigby in surreal slacker misadventures.

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Seeley's 2025 mini sending Rogue into the Savage Land.

subject: series
synopsis: Akihisa Ikeda's harem manga follows ordinary human Tsukune accidentally enrolling in a school for monsters and being protected by a vampire girl. A popular but lightweight entry in the monster-girl harem genre.
author: Akihisa Ikeda

subject: series
synopsis: Sean Lewis and Benjamin Mackey's Image series: a heavy-metal guitarist discovers he is the reincarnation of a Catholic saint, drafted into a holy war.

subject: series
synopsis: Epic Collection trade paperbacks reprinting classic Silver Surfer stories from Stan Lee and Jack Kirby through subsequent runs, collecting the Sentinel of the Spaceways' cosmic adventures and philosophical meditations on humanity.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Buccellato and Toni Infante's Image series follows Travis, a young man searching for his birth father, who uncovers ties to a charismatic cult and its murderous legacy. A twin-timeline thriller about destiny and inherited violence.
author: Brian Buccellato

subject: series
synopsis: Eric Peterson and Joe Aubrey's hilariously violent sci-fi satire following the Intergalactic Postal Service's team of delivery workers — competitive, murderous contractors in a cosmos that runs on capitalism and chaos.
author: Eric Peterson

subject: series
synopsis: The New 52 Star-Spangled War Stories (2014): Palmiotti and Gray's G.I. Zombie, an undead soldier working undercover.

subject: series
synopsis: The concluding chapter of the Battle of Jakku storyline, depicting the Empire's final desperate stand on the desert planet and the New Republic's decisive victory that ended the Galactic Civil War.

subject: series
synopsis: Tini Howard's short-lived Marvel series assembling a black-ops team to handle supernatural threats the Avengers can't publicly acknowledge, with a solid cast in a concept that didn't find its audience before cancellation.
author: Tini Howard

subject: series
synopsis: Roy Thomas's DC science fiction series following a team of colonizers in conflict with alien powers across the outer solar system. A Bronze Age space opera with adventure-serial pacing.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Nick Spencer's 2011 DC revival of the classic Tower Comics team — The Higher United Nations Defense Enforcement Reserves — given a modern espionage treatment exploring the cost of superhuman power on the agents who wield it. A sharp update that honored the property's history.
author: Nick Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Bronze Age black-and-white horror magazine featuring Simon Garth, the zombie of Haiti, alongside Brother Voodoo and related supernatural stories. Written by Tony Isabella, Steve Gerber, and others, it brought literary ambition to a grindhouse format.
author: Tony Isabella

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's archival collections of classic Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles comics from the original Mirage era, preserving the darker, grittier original stories that predated the franchise's mainstream success.
author: Kevin Eastman

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison and Keith Giffen's fill-in arc written to bridge a gap in The Authority's publication history, sending the team through alternate realities after an attack. An unusual curiosity — Morrison's Authority concepts are intriguing but the book's purpose as a gap-filler limits its ambitions.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: A noir crime story set in a Prohibition-era world of demons and monsters, where a two-bit criminal cursed with resurrection is used as a pawn by competing supernatural mob families.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2020 digital-first Flash anthology, Barry Allen stories by Gail Simone, Jeff Parker and others.

subject: series
synopsis: Defiant Comics' superhero team title, featuring a group of empowered individuals in the Defiant universe. One of the publisher's longer-running series before Defiant's 1994 collapse, showing Shooter's ambition for a tightly-plotted shared universe.
author: Jim Shooter

subject: series
synopsis: Collected editions of Francois Schuiten and Benoit Peeters' European graphic novel series — Les Cites Obscures — a rich alternate-history world of strange cities and their extraordinary inhabitants.
author: Benoit Peeters

subject: series
synopsis: Yuyuko Takemiya's high school romantic comedy manga adaptation follows the unexpected partnership of a gentle boy and a ferociously tiny girl called the Palmtop Tiger as they help each other pursue their crushes. One of the definitive tsundere romances.
author: Yuyuko Takemiya

subject: series
synopsis: Bendis, Straczynski and Loeb's 2006 crossover pitting the Ultimate Universe heroes against the Squadron Supreme.

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Gray and Roger Cruz's 2009 all-ages-style series set in the early days of the Giant-Size X-Men team.
author: Scott Gray

subject: series
synopsis: Chester Brown's experimental dream-diary comic from the mid-1990s — dense, surreal, and deeply personal. Published before 'Louis Riel' and 'Paying For It,' this harder-to-find work reveals the idiosyncratic formal experiments Brown was conducting before finding his documentary voice.
author: Chester Brown

subject: series
synopsis: Early collected volumes of Stan Sakai's samurai rabbit classic, one of the greatest long-running indie comics.
author: Stan Sakai

subject: series
synopsis: A recent Vampirella series exploring themes of identity and duality through dark supernatural horror, featuring the vampire heroine confronting mirror-world threats and aspects of her own nature.

subject: series
synopsis: A golden-age Marvel (Timely) series following Venus, the goddess of love, in a unique blend of mythology, romance, and horror as she descends to Earth and becomes involved in mortal affairs.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Boom Studios' comics featuring WWE wrestlers in stories that blend real-world professional wrestling characters with action-comic storytelling.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Hiroaki Samura's (Blade of the Immortal) comedy manga following Minare Koda, a hot-headed restaurant worker in Sapporo whose ranting monologue is secretly recorded by a radio producer and broadcast — launching her accidental career as a late-night radio host. Samura's signature intensity channeled into hilarious character comedy.
author: Hiroaki Samura

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's five-issue mini revisiting the Days of Future Past alternate timeline from the perspective of the Weapon X program and its test subjects. Connects two iconic X-Men concepts with mixed results.

subject: series
synopsis: Christos Gage's 2024 mini: a team of Wolverine variants from across the multiverse.

subject: series
synopsis: Sean Ruffner and Brett Booth's 1997 Wildstorm series continuing Backlash's covert team.
author: Sean Ruffner

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Mignola and Chris Roberson's installment of the Witchfinder series featuring Sir Edward Grey's Victorian occult investigations, exploring connections between spiritualism, secret societies, and Lovecraftian horror within the Hellboy universe. Confident Mignola-verse storytelling.
author: Chris Roberson

subject: series
synopsis: A five-issue Wolverine story stranding Logan on a mysterious island filled with strange fauna and survival challenges, offering a stripped-down premise that plays to the character's primal nature.
author: Bruce Jones

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Epic Collection reprint line presenting Wolverine's classic adventures in chronological order, including the landmark Chris Claremont and Frank Miller miniseries and essential Bronze/Copper Age stories that defined the character.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Simon Spurrier's sardonic mini-series spotlighting the Science Team as they attempt to create a space elevator and encounter unexpected threats.
author: Simon Spurrier

subject: series
synopsis: Roger Stern's Marvel miniseries pits the X-Men against the Avengers as both pursue a depowered Magneto, who is put on trial for his crimes while the wreckage of a Master Mold sentinel threatens everyone. A morally knotty clash over justice and redemption.
author: Roger Stern

subject: series
synopsis: A five-issue X-Men event mini-series by Chris Claremont revisiting Magik and Limbo, pitting the X-Men against Belasco with classic X-Men horror-fantasy stakes. A solid Claremont return to X-Men mythology he helped define.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Daniel Pecqueur and Nicolas Malfin's French SF: the billionaire owner of a floating city for the rich is framed and cast out among the poor below.

subject: series
synopsis: A Deadpool and Wolverine miniseries; rival anti-hero dynamic.

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Capullo and Todd McFarlane's long-anticipated 2022 crossover between Batman and Spawn — two characters whose mid-1990s cultural dominance overlapped dramatically — finding a satisfying supernatural threat for the dark knight to confront alongside McFarlane's anti-hero. A crowd-pleasing event for fans of either property.
author: Greg Capullo, Todd McFarlane

subject: series
synopsis: Yashichiro Takagi's manga adaptation of Fujino Omori's light novel, following Bell Cranel as he adventures in a dungeon beneath the city of Orario, seeking to grow strong enough to be worthy of the stronger heroes around him. A competent isekai-adjacent fantasy that spawned a popular anime series.
author: Fujino Omori (story)

subject: series
synopsis: The Deluxe Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe (1985-1988), the encyclopedia of Marvel characters with schematic art.

subject: series
synopsis: Boom Studios' 2019 relaunch reimagines Buffy Summers in a modern setting — a new continuity updating the mythology for a contemporary audience while honoring the core characters and themes of the original show.
author: Jordie Bellaire

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Gerber's cult 1990 series reviving the Foolkiller concept through a new bearer of the identity, and Max Bemis's 2016 revival as a psychotherapist who secretly kills patients he deems irredeemable — a dark satirical take on vigilantism.
author: Steve Gerber

subject: series
synopsis: Len Strazewski and Mike Parobeck's 1992 Justice Society of America: the Golden Age heroes, back from limbo, adapt to the 1990s.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's oversized quarterly anthology exploring stories outside regular continuity, often featuring high-profile artists. Best known for early issues with George Pérez and other top talents of the 1990s.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Kara Zor-El's first solo series (1972-1974), college-girl adventures with a Zatanna backup.
author: Cary Bates, Len Wein

subject: series
synopsis: The Archie/MLJ superhero The Black Hood across various publishers — a masked vigilante crimefighter who passed from the golden-age Red Circle imprint through revivals at DC and Dark Circle. The character's longevity reflects both nostalgia and the interesting hook of an everyman cop turned vigilante.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Phil Hester's run on Top Cow's The Darkness following Jackie Estacado as he deals with the consequences of his power, featuring the gothic horror-crime mythology of the franchise.
author: Phil Hester

subject: series
synopsis: The 1999 M-Tech Warlock: the techno-organic New Mutant revived in a short, poorly received series.

subject: series
synopsis: Motoro Mase's dystopian manga: in a Japan where one in a thousand citizens is fated to die at 24, a civil servant delivers the death notices.

subject: series
synopsis: Fleetway's 1950s pocket digest of detective and SF strips, starring heroes like Blackshirt and Lesley Shane.

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' complete Don Rosa Duck stories, including The Life and Times of Scrooge McDuck.

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander's original Suicide Squad (1987-1992): Amanda Waller's Task Force X sends convicts on deniable missions.

subject: series
synopsis: Skottie Young's 2022 return of I Hate Fairyland: Gert is back in Fairyland as an adult in Gert's Inferno and beyond.
author: Skottie Young

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan's 2015 Uncanny Avengers: Steve Rogers's Unity Squad of Avengers, X-Men and Inhumans with Deadpool.
author: Gerry Duggan

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jurgens's Rebirth Batman Beyond: Terry McGinnis protects Neo-Gotham, through Brainiac and the Jokerz.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1996 Journey into Mystery revival as a rotating feature book (Black Knight, Shang-Chi, Hannibal King).

subject: series
synopsis: Saladin Ahmed's 2019 Miles Morales: Spider-Man, Miles juggling Brooklyn Visions Academy and the Assessor's clone scheme.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Allor's 2019 IDW G.I. Joe: a Cobra-ruled world where a ragtag resistance carries on the fight.

subject: series
synopsis: The Rebirth Aquaman (2016-2021): Dan Abnett's Atlantis politics, then Kelly Sue DeConnick and Robson Rocha's amnesiac Arthur.

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Carey's Dynamite Barbarella, the space adventuress's revived galactic escapades.

subject: series
synopsis: John Ridley's Black Panther run; contemporary socially-conscious superhero storytelling.
author: John Ridley

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron and Chris Bachalo's 2015 Doctor Strange: magic has a price, and the Empirikul set out to burn it from every dimension.

subject: series
synopsis: Wildstorm's 1995 Grifter ongoing: Cole Cash as a lone gun-for-hire after WildC.A.T.s.
author: Steven T. Seagle

subject: series
synopsis: Rafer Roberts and Mike Norton's Albatross comedy about a lowlife private eye turned into a pug, on the run from demons.

subject: series
synopsis: Fabian Nicieza's 1992 Nomad: Jack Monroe, Bucky's successor, drifts across America with a baby in tow.
author: Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: Kevin J. Anderson's 2004 Starjammers mini: Corsair's space pirates against the Shi'ar.
author: Kevin J. Anderson

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's second Saturday Morning Adventures run: the 1987-cartoon Turtles in new episodic adventures.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1969 Phantom Stranger: the enigmatic wanderer battles occult evil, with Jim Aparo art later in the run.

subject: series
synopsis: Donny Cates and Ryan Stegman's 2018 Venom: Eddie Brock uncovers Knull, the god of symbiotes, leading to Absolute Carnage and King in Black.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's 2018 Xena: Warrior Princess, Xena and Gabrielle in new adventures from the TV series.

subject: series
synopsis: Rob Liefeld's Image-launch Youngblood: a government-sponsored celebrity super-team, all pouches, guns and splash pages.

subject: series
synopsis: The New Mutants annuals (1984-1991), including Psylocke's American debut in #2.
author: Louise Jones Simonson, Peter Sanderson

subject: series
synopsis: Hirohiko Araki's Part 3: Jotaro Kujo and his grandfather Joseph travel from Japan to Egypt with their Stands to defeat the vampire Dio.

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Bagge's annual continuation of Hate: Buddy Bradley's misadventures as a married man and father in New Jersey.

subject: series
synopsis: Archie's 2015 relaunch: Mark Waid and Fiona Staples reimagine Riverdale with a modern, serialized teen dramedy, later Nick Spencer.

subject: series
synopsis: G. Willow Wilson's 2014 Ms. Marvel: Jersey City teen Kamala Khan gains shape-shifting powers and becomes a hero, drawn by Adrian Alphona and Takeshi Miyazawa.
author: G. Willow Wilson

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Hale Fialkov's Oni series in which the afterlife has fallen into chaos and the souls of the dead fight back.

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Hogan and Chris Sprouse's 2010 Tom Strong mini: Tom faces an alternate Millennium City ruled by robots.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's omnibus reprints of B.P.R.D., Mignola, Arcudi and Guy Davis's horror epic of the Bureau's war against the frog plague and Hell on Earth.

subject: series
synopsis: A chibi gag spinoff of Bungo Stray Dogs, the Agency and Port Mafia in short comedy strips.

subject: series
synopsis: Kenzer and Company spinoff of Knights of the Dinner Table, comic adventures of the Hackmaster RPG world.

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' late-1980s alternative comics anthology.

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak's 2025 comic based on the TV series Supernatural, the Winchester brothers hunting monsters.
author: Greg Pak

subject: series
synopsis: Mamoru Nagano's baroque space opera of the Joker star cluster, where living Fatimas pilot giant Mortar Headd mechs for knights and kings.

subject: series
synopsis: Annual summer anthology specials from 2000AD featuring new and classic strips, artist showcases, and standalone stories that provide an excellent cross-section of the anthology's house style and stable of characters.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Four-part companion to 52 depicting Black Adam's devastating rampage across the globe.
author: Keith Champagne

subject: series
synopsis: Wildstorm's limited series adaptation of the Nightmare on Elm Street franchise, following Freddy Krueger in new dream-invasion scenarios. A competent licensed horror series that can't fully escape the limitations of adapting a film franchise.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Rick Geary's ongoing true crime graphic novel series meticulously reconstructing famous Victorian-era murders — the Lizzie Borden case, Jack the Ripper, and others — with painstaking historical research and deadpan illustration.
author: Rick Geary

subject: series
synopsis: Tsutomu Nihei's sci-fi manga set on the artificial world of Aposimz, where the surface is frozen and deadly and the surviving human remnants fight Frame disease, which transforms people into machine-creature hybrids. Nihei's distinctive environmental design and austere post-apocalyptic aesthetics are as compelling here as in Blame!
author: Tsutomu Nihei

subject: series
synopsis: Jerry Prosser and Kelley Jones's 1992 Aliens mini: an android-led crew raids a xenomorph hive to harvest royal jelly.
author: Jerry Prosser

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' anthology revival series reprinting and presenting new stories featuring golden age superhero characters, maintaining AC's dedication to preserving and celebrating classic American superhero history.

subject: series
synopsis: Collected volumes of Scott Snyder and Rafael Albuquerque's American Vampire, charting a new breed of vampire uniquely born of American violence and ambition across different eras of U.S. history.
author: Scott Snyder

subject: series
synopsis: Kazu Kibuishi's all-ages fantasy series follows Emily and Navin Hayes who discover their late great-grandfather's magical amulet, drawing them into the fantastical underground world of Alledia where Emily must become its guardian.
author: Kazu Kibuishi

subject: series
synopsis: Marc Bernardin and Shawn Martinbrough's 2024 adaptation of Neil Gaiman's novel: Fat Charlie discovers his late father was the trickster god Anansi.

subject: series
synopsis: A reprint collection series collecting Steve Engelhart's run on the West Coast Avengers, featuring the California-based spinoff team with Hawkeye, Mockingbird, Wonder Man, and Iron Man, including key storylines like Lost in Space-Time.
author: Roger Stern

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Mignola and Christopher Golden's dark supernatural adventure series collected in omnibus form, following Lord Henry Baltimore's obsessive pursuit of the vampire who cursed him across a plague-ravaged alternate World War I Europe.
author: Mike Mignola

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's 2012 conclusion to his seven-year Batman epic, featuring Batman Inc. — the network of international Batman operatives — facing Talia al Ghul's Leviathan organization in a war that ends with catastrophic personal costs. Morrison's finale paid off every thread he'd planted since 2006 in one of the most ambitious and emotionally devastating runs in Batman history.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Yukito Kishiro's cyberpunk classic: a doctor revives the cyborg girl Alita from a scrapyard, and she becomes a bounty hunter and Motorball star beneath the sky city.

subject: series
synopsis: Yukito Kishiro's ambitious sequel to the original Battle Angel Alita, sending cyborg warrior Alita/Gally to the orbital city of Tiphares and into the ZOTT tournament that spans the solar system. While narratively denser and more complex than the original, it retains Kishiro's extraordinary visual imagination and pushes the mythology to epic scale.
author: Yukito Kishiro

subject: series
synopsis: Yukito Kishiro's sequel series expanding Alita's backstory on Mars, revealing the traumatic origins that shaped the cyborg warrior before her life in the Scrapyard. Dense cyberpunk mythology with Kishiro's signature detailed mechanical artwork.
author: Yukito Kishiro

subject: series
synopsis: The English-language Cinebook edition of Jean Roba's classic Belgian humour series Boule et Bill, following the warm and funny misadventures of a red-haired boy and his lovable cocker spaniel. A beloved all-ages staple of Franco-Belgian comics since the 1960s.
author: Jean Roba

subject: series
synopsis: Rei Hiroe's stylish action thriller follows a Japanese salaryman kidnapped and absorbed into a crew of mercenary pirates operating in the lawless Southeast Asian port city of Roanapur. Known for its exceptional gun-fu action choreography and fascinating cast of morally complex criminals.
author: Rei Hiroe

subject: series
synopsis: A modern mature-readers Blade series with the Red Band designation indicating more visceral vampire-hunting content, positioning the character firmly in horror territory for contemporary audiences.
author: Bryan Hill

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Lemire's 2015 Bloodshot Reborn: freed of his nanites, Ray Garrison is haunted by hallucinations as a new wave of nanite killers emerges.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's Buffy Season 11 (2016): a mystical disaster in San Francisco leads the government to round up the supernatural.
author: Christos N. Gage

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Lafler's comic about a jazz band of insects in a 1950s bebop city, struggling with music, drugs and fame.

subject: series
synopsis: Fred Van Lente's Marvel prequel tie-in to the Captain America: The First Avenger film, providing backstory for key characters before their movie appearances. Competent promotional material that expands on the film's world without demanding independent attention.
author: Fred Van Lente

subject: series
synopsis: Jackson Lanzing and Collin Kelly's run reimagines Steve Rogers as a symbol being actively weaponized against its own ideals, mixing spy thriller plotting with earnest examination of American mythology -- ambitious and uneven but more interesting than the average Cap book.
author: Jackson Lanzing

subject: series
synopsis: A Franco-Belgian western series following a Chinese immigrant navigating violence, racism, and survival in the 19th-century American frontier. Written and drawn by Tiburce Oger with gritty realism and an outsider's perspective on the myth of the West.
author: Tiburce Oger

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1970s anthology evolving from Tower of Shadows into a series featuring Thongor the Barbarian, Man-Wolf, and other fantasy and horror characters. Part of Marvel's broad bronze-age genre expansion beyond superheroes.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Gruenwald's 1986 Marvel New Universe series about seven people with powers who try to live quietly while being hunted, one of the more humanistic entries in Marvel's ambitious but ultimately failed New Universe initiative.
author: Mark Gruenwald

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2018 promotional magazine with previews and short stories setting up its upcoming publishing.

subject: series
synopsis: Dwayne McDuffie's beloved satirical comedy about the company responsible for cleaning up after superhero battles in the Marvel Universe.
author: Dwayne McDuffie

subject: series
synopsis: Andy Kubert's 2013 Elseworlds-style DC story showing a future where Damian Wayne has become Batman after Bruce's death, exploring his more ruthless approach to justice and his slow growth toward the standard his father set. Kubert's art was the primary draw of this otherwise familiar story.
author: Andy Kubert

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and David Mack's eight-issue prestige series depicting the final days and death of Matt Murdock, told through the perspective of reporter Ben Urich investigating what Daredevil's last words meant. A gorgeous, novelistic meditation on legacy and the cost of a life spent fighting that ranks among the best Daredevil stories ever told.
author: Brian Michael Bendis, David Mack

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1992 series about Chris Powell, a teenager who discovers an amulet that transforms him into Darkhawk — a powerful android body with mysterious alien origins. A product of the early 90s teen-hero wave, the series featured solid action and slow revelation of the Darkhawk armor's cosmic backstory.
author: Danny Fingeroth

subject: series
synopsis: A companion miniseries to the Death of Wolverine event exploring how Logan's death reverberates through the lives of those he left behind — allies, enemies, and the many people shaped by his influence.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Lee and Brandon Choi's Wildstorm/Image series starring Michael Cray, a black ops soldier with supernatural resilience who operates outside government sanction. Blends military thriller aesthetics with superhero action in the early Image house style.
author: Brandon Choi

subject: series
synopsis: Jack Kirby's 1978 Marvel series about Devil, a massive red Tyrannosaurus, and his young companion Moon-Boy in a prehistoric valley filled with strange creatures and cavemen. Kirby's unfettered imagination working at full tilt — absurd, vibrant, and irresistible in its primitive energy.
author: Jack Kirby

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Shooter's 2010 Dark Horse revival of Gold Key's Doctor Solar, Man of the Atom.

subject: series
synopsis: Nanashi's popular manga about an older boy who gets teased by the spirited younger girl Nagatoro, evolving from embarrassment-comedy into a genuine mutual affection. A crowd-pleasing romcom that helped define a modern manga subgenre.
author: Nanashi

subject: series
synopsis: Christophe Arleston and Alessandro Barbucci's fantasy comedy set on Ekho, a mirror Earth of dragons, fairies and talking animals.

subject: series
synopsis: Kei Sanbe's mystery manga following Satoru Fujinuma, a struggling manga artist with the involuntary ability to travel back moments in time to prevent tragedies, who is thrust 18 years into the past to prevent the child murders that shaped his childhood. A masterfully constructed thriller that balances supernatural premise with deeply felt human drama.
author: Kei Sanbe

subject: series
synopsis: Collected editions of John Byrne's landmark 1981-1986 Fantastic Four run, which redefined the team's dynamics and added significant mythology -- among the most influential superhero runs of the Bronze Age and essential reading for any FF fan.
author: John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: A tie-in miniseries to the Fear Itself event spotlighting the eight Worthy, mortal warriors empowered by Serpent's enchanted hammers to serve as his heralds of destruction across the Marvel Universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Tom DeFalco's 1986 Marvel limited series introducing Firestar as a solo hero separate from the New Warriors context, following Angelica Jones' origin at Emma Frost's Massachusetts Academy. An important series for establishing Firestar's backstory and her complicated history with the White Queen.
author: Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and Andy Kubert's landmark 2011 DC event that gave rise to the New 52 relaunch — a time-altered world where Thomas Wayne is Batman, Aquaman and Wonder Woman are at war, and Barry Allen must find a way to restore the proper timeline. A dense, effective superhero thriller with a genuinely emotional core.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1994 Avengers spinoff featuring Iron Man, Scarlet Witch, Spider-Woman, and U.S. Agent as a proactive rapid-response team operating out of the Chaos Computes facility. A transitional book between the West Coast Avengers cancellation and the standard Avengers line.
author: Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning

subject: series
synopsis: Tohru Fujisawa's beloved manga about Eikichi Onizuka, a former gang member who becomes a high school teacher through sheer force of personality and unconventional methods. Combines raucous comedy with genuine emotional warmth and surprisingly thoughtful examination of Japan's educational pressures; a classic of the late 1990s shonen era.
author: Tohru Fujisawa

subject: series
synopsis: Collected edition of Greg Weisman's Gargoyles comic continuation following the Manhattan Clan.
author: Greg Weisman

subject: series
synopsis: A sci-fi spinoff of the Geronimo Stilton franchise set in outer space, featuring mouse characters on cosmic adventures. Designed for young readers in the same appealing visual style as the main series.
author: Geronimo Stilton

subject: series
synopsis: Len Wein and Dave Cockrum's landmark 1975 one-shot that launched the All-New, All-Different X-Men team — Wolverine, Storm, Colossus, Nightcrawler, Thunderbird, Banshee, and Sunfire — rescuing the original team from Krakoa. One of the most historically significant comics ever published.
author: Len Wein

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's Eric Powell and Tracy Marsh-written Godzilla series showing the real-world chaos that would ensue if Godzilla and other kaiju actually emerged in modern society — a ground-level perspective on the monster invasion that balanced horror with dark comedy.
author: Eric Powell, Tracy Marsh

subject: series
synopsis: Sam Humphries' 2016 series pairing rookie Green Lanterns Jessica Cruz and Simon Baz — two characters brought together precisely because their personalities clash — as they cover for Hal Jordan while he's away. Humphries' skill at character comedy and genuine superhero emotion made this the best GL book of the Rebirth era.
author: Sam Humphries

subject: series
synopsis: Max Landis and Giuseppe Camuncoli's Image miniseries about a band of medieval knights investigating supernatural disappearances in a peaceful valley, with a twist that fundamentally recontextualizes the story. An effective genre subversion that Camuncoli's beautifully rendered art elevates considerably.
author: Max Landis

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's anthology series pairing the Guardians of the Galaxy with various Earth heroes, serving as team-up entertainment during the Bendis Guardians era. Light but entertaining cosmic superhero fun.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Valerio Schiti's 2016 relaunched Guardians series following All-New All-Different Marvel, featuring an expanded roster including Kitty Pryde (as Star-Lord), Agent Venom, and Groot. A solid entry in Bendis's long Guardians run with improved art.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Kyle Higgins and Alec Siegel's locked-room murder mystery in deep space — an investigator is sent to a generation ship to solve a death that may involve his ex-wife. Tight mystery plotting with a strong visual sensibility.
author: Kyle Higgins, Alec Siegel
